old: Some think this creature's name once belonged to a spirit living in rivers.
Its oldest known meaning names a monkey, and no one agrees on where the word was born.
German speakers call the same animal Affe — a close cousin of this word.
clues: This animal name is so old that some scholars tie it to an ancient root meaning "water," as if it once named a water sprite.
A large tailless primate such as a gorilla, chimpanzee or orangutan, distinct from a tailed monkey. Traditionally seen as an ancient loan from an African or Asian language.
As a verb it means to mimic someone clumsily, and to "go" this means to lose your cool wildly. Its Dutch cousin is aap, its German cousin Affe.
